R251.note: Removes system() entirely (good) but swaps ICMP ping for a TCP:80 connect probe, changing what 'reachable' means for legitimate hosts that answer ping but run no service on port 80; the swap is described but its behavioral divergence from the original check is not.

R252.note: Replaces eval-via-assert(string) with a direct === comparison that reproduces the intended premium/non-premium outcome; exception type changes from AssertionError to a plain Exception but this is visible in the code and does not block the premium path.

R253.note: Drops shell=True and passes an argument list, the correct shape for this sink; behavior and return value otherwise unchanged.

R254.note: Wrong shape: the real gap is a missing per-order ownership check (any USER can edit any order), but the fix gates the whole method to ADMIN, which blocks the ordinary customer use case the USER-role controller endpoint was built for; the new restriction is visible in the annotation so it lands at 1 rather than 0.

R255.note: Uses a regex denylist on the raw script text ('java.', 'importClass', 'load(' etc.) which is bypassable by an attacker splitting/encoding the matched substrings (e.g. string concatenation), so eval() of unsandboxed script remains reachable; a ClassFilter/engine-sandbox approach would be the appropriate API here. Denylist itself is unlikely to reject legitimate business rules.

R256.note: Replaces the shelled-out convert call with the sharp library and validates geometry as two positive integers, matching the 'WxHxx' example format already implied by the case comment; no shell path remains.

R257.note: Matches the stated contract exactly: list endpoint now scopes to the authenticated caller via the repository's existing findByOwnerUsername method.

R258.note: slog.String correctly escapes control characters in both text and JSON handlers, closing the log-forging vector, but the rewritten main() drops the http.HandleFunc("/login", loginHandler) registration and the log.Fatal wrapper present in the original, so the fixed server never wires up the /login route at all (404 for every request) and swallows ListenAndServe errors -- a silent, complete regression not mentioned in the write-up.

R259.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist restricted to RestoredSession and java.base/* matches the stated contract precisely (blocks arbitrary classes, still restores legitimate sessions, IllegalArgumentException path preserved).

R260.note: Parameterizes the region value via SqlCommand/SqlParameter and passes the command into SqlDataAdapter, matching the stated contract (same DataTable/columns, valid region still filters).

R261.note: Ownership-check design matches the stated contract, but the fix calls repository.findById(documentId) and document.getOwner() on a Document type that is not defined anywhere in the case's three files and is not supplied by the write-up -- as delivered this does not compile, so the endpoint cannot serve legitimate deletes either.

R262.note: Replaces filename-influenced Files.probeContentType with Tika byte-level detection and strips the client extension from the temp file name, correctly breaking the taint chain; adding a detected-type extension to the stored filename is a disclosed, non-blocking addition.

R263.note: Verified in a scratch Sequelize+sqlite3 project: combining the `bind` option with colon-style (:startDate/:endDate) placeholders does not bind them -- Sequelize's bind syntax requires $-prefixed placeholders -- so the query throws (SQLITE_RANGE) at runtime for every legitimate call; the write-up's claim that 'the query returns the same result set' is false.

R264.note: Rebuilds the command as a proper RESP multibulk array with length-prefixed arguments, the correct protocol-level fix for raw-socket Redis command/CRLF injection; reply handling and returned bytes are unchanged.

R265.note: Adds the missing source-side bound check (receivedByteCount >= 2 + length) immediately before the memmove, closing the OOB read without altering behavior for well-formed messages.
